observations.behavior: Adds a new utility to identify and extract command labels that exactly match the user's search query.
observations.posthog_connection: This could improve discoverability in PostHog Desktop by surfacing precise commands immediately rather than burying them among partial matches.

observations.behavior: Changes how command results are ordered. Puts exact matches at the top of the list before other relevant results.
observations.posthog_connection: Makes it faster for users to find specific commands they typed without scrolling past unrelated options.

observations.behavior: Replaces an inline substring matching implementation with a dedicated helper function, while also removing the explicit whitespace handling from this hunk.
observations.posthog_connection: Standardizes command searching behavior across the application; however, note that the removed local implementation did not handle surrounding whitespace, whereas the added global helper does.

observations.limitations: The patch lacks tests or documentation explaining why exact-match prioritization is preferred over simple relevance ranking. No release notes indicate adoption or performance impact. The removal of whitespace trimming in H3 suggests either redundancy or incomplete migration, requiring further inspection.

review.reason: Substantive improvement: adds exact-matching and reordering capabilities to command discovery, demonstrated through new utility functions and their use in CommandMenu. This could help PostHog Desktop users complete workflows more efficiently by surfacing precise commands first.
review.posthog_relevance: Could improve discoverability and workflow efficiency in PostHog Desktop's command palette.
review.uncertainty: Without broader context on how command search currently behaves or user expectations, it remains unclear whether exact-prioritization outweighs other heuristics. Also no test results are shown.
